pages.heading: Following the coast
pages.body: A KNCraft coastline. Shorelines can offer useful landmarks for a long journey.

pages.heading: A riverside landmark
pages.body: A stone circle near the river. Distinctive structures help you recognize a route.

pages.heading: Below the surface
pages.body: A large marine animal beneath the water. Leave space when exploring by boat.

pages.heading: Read the landscape
pages.body: Several mods shape the same journey. Tectonic controls broad terrain forms; Terralith adds biome variety using vanilla blocks; Biomes O' Plenty adds its own biomes and materials. Structure mods place places to investigate along the way. Distant

pages.heading: Read the landscape (cont.)
pages.body: Horizons changes how far terrain can be seen. It does not create mountains or structures. This chapter includes author examples and captures from KNCraft. Credits identify their source; scenery does not guarantee what you

pages.heading: Read the landscape (cont.)
pages.body: will find along another route.

pages.heading: Under the mountain
pages.body: A river runs beneath the terrain. Bring light and mark the entrance.

pages.heading: Tectonic
pages.body: Expect large changes in elevation, substantial ranges and terrain that can turn a short straight-line journey into a long route. Look for valleys, river corridors and manageable passes before climbing. Underground rivers

pages.heading: Tectonic (cont.)
pages.body: add another kind of route, but visibility and return access matter. Check that an apparent tunnel continues before moving animals or a loaded party into it.

pages.heading: Mountain routes
pages.body: Tectonic's mountain-range example. A valley route may be faster

pages.heading: Mountain routes
pages.body: and easier to retreat along than a direct climb. Keep temperature and weather in mind when choosing a pass.

pages.heading: Underground rivers
pages.body: Tectonic's underground-river example. Light the entry and keep a

pages.heading: Underground rivers
pages.body: clear return route before exploring out of sight.

pages.heading: Terralith
pages.body: Terralith rearranges vanilla materials into a wider set of realistic and unusual biomes. Color alone may not tell you what a surface is made from; inspect blocks when gathering resources. Use distinctive landforms as route markers, but record a

pages.heading: Terralith (cont.)
pages.body: return location too. Terrain that is easy to recognize in daylight can be hard to read through rain or snow.

pages.heading: Terralith landscape
pages.body: An author-gallery example of contrasting terrain and materials. It

pages.heading: Terralith landscape
pages.body: illustrates the variety of the project; your KNCraft route will depend on the seed and the other generation mods.

pages.heading: Wildlife in open country
pages.body: Animals share the open landscape. Leave room to observe before

pages.heading: Wildlife in open country
pages.body: approaching.

pages.heading: Biomes O' Plenty
pages.body: Biomes O' Plenty brings additional vegetation, wood types and other building materials alongside its biomes. Collect saplings when you find a useful wood, rather than filling your entire travel inventory with logs. Keep new materials

pages.heading: Biomes O' Plenty (cont.)
pages.body: organized by purpose. A new-looking biome can also change your temperature situation, so check before making it your next camp.

pages.heading: Redwood forest
pages.body: Redwood Forest from the project gallery. Tall vegetation limits sightlines at ground

pages.heading: Redwood forest
pages.body: level and can hide the route back to your group.

pages.heading: An entrance in the ruins
pages.body: An opening beneath weathered stonework. Check the way back before descending.

pages.heading: Inside the dungeon
pages.body: A spawner and chests inside the structure. Secure a route out before searching.

pages.heading: Across the water
pages.body: A large ship on the ocean. Scout an approach before boarding.

pages.heading: Dungeons Enhanced
pages.body: Dungeons Enhanced adds separate medieval and fantasy structures, including towers, ships and larger complexes. A visible building is not proof of safe shelter. Approach with light, space for loot and a route out. Clear a manageable area

pages.heading: Dungeons Enhanced (cont.)
pages.body: before continuing farther inside. Check the map between stops so a long search does not leave the storm closing on your exit.

pages.heading: A structure offshore
pages.body: The project's Pirate Ship example. Scout the water and the deck before committing

pages.heading: A structure offshore
pages.body: to a landing; aquatic wildlife can complicate the approach.

pages.heading: Structory
pages.body: Structory adds smaller ruins, cottages, graveyards and other signs of past habitation. These work as landmarks and short stops between larger objectives. Examine the surroundings before treating a ruin as a campsite. A

pages.heading: Structory (cont.)
pages.body: broken wall may offer cover, but it may not provide the roof or temperature control you need.

pages.heading: Ruins along the route
pages.body: Grassy Ruins from Structory's gallery. Use a distinctive ruin to describe a meeting

pages.heading: Ruins along the route
pages.body: point, then give its coordinates to avoid confusion.

pages.heading: Abridged
pages.body: Abridged adds bridges over rivers and larger gaps. They can save building time and make a useful meeting point. Check both ends, the deck and the inhabitants before crossing. The author notes that bridge placement can behave oddly with terrain

pages.heading: Abridged (cont.)
pages.body: mods such as Tectonic. Do not drive a train or lead animals onto a crossing simply because it looks complete from far away.

pages.heading: A canyon crossing
pages.body: Abridged's stone-bridge example. Inspect the actual crossing before using

pages.heading: A canyon crossing
pages.body: it as the only evacuation route.

pages.heading: Towns and Towers
pages.body: Towns and Towers adds village, outpost and ship designs inspired by varied architecture. Identify whether a location is friendly before walking into its center. A settlement can provide supplies or a useful landmark, but it remains exposed to

pages.heading: Towns and Towers (cont.)
pages.body: the world around it. Keep villagers out of harm's way and leave routes open if your group uses the area as a staging point.

pages.heading: A different village layout
pages.body: Birch Forest Village from the project gallery. Larger or unfamiliar layouts

pages.heading: A different village layout
pages.body: make it worth choosing a clear entrance and meeting place.

pages.heading: Distant Horizons
pages.body: Distant Horizons displays simplified distant terrain. KNCraft supports it server-side, but your view still depends on the client setup and available terrain data. Allow time for distant areas to fill in. Use the view to choose a general direction,

pages.heading: Distant Horizons (cont.)
pages.body: then inspect the ground as you approach. It is not a live scan for mobs, loot, intact bridges or every recent block change. Use BlueMap for the server's Wither Storm markers.

pages.heading: The distant landscape
pages.body: The owner's Distant Horizons view. Distant terrain is not a live view of every hazard.

pages.heading: Distant Horizons off
pages.body: The overlook without Distant Horizons. Compare the distant terrain in the next

pages.heading: Distant Horizons off
pages.body: view.

pages.heading: Distant Horizons on
pages.body: Distant terrain extends beyond the nearby chunks. Camera and lighting

pages.heading: Distant Horizons on
pages.body: differ slightly.

pages.heading: Before going farther
pages.body: Choose your next stopping point while you still have enough food, temperature supplies and daylight or lighting to reach it. Record a discovered Waystone and check the map before changing your route. Bring back useful ingredients and

pages.heading: Before going farther (cont.)
pages.body: information, not just a full inventory. A marked passage, working bridge or prepared camp can be worth more on the next journey than another stack of stone.

pages.heading: More accomplishments
pages.body: The journal now includes BOP's native all-biomes achievement and RopeBridge's two builder-item and two construction achievements. All 344 records remain independent. Build or explore at your own pace; nothing requires completing the whole journal.

pages.heading: Equipment bonuses travel with you
pages.body: Furor, Agility, Range and Armoring keep their native strengths while contributing alongside other attribute bonuses. Changing or removing equipment updates the bonus. Wing armor effects still recognize your active Elytra Slot wings.

pages.heading: Record the journey
pages.body: The FTB journal tracks individual landmarks, bosses and native mod advancements. Structure records update when you enter a landmark after this update. They grant no loot or recipe unlocks. Use them as a travel checklist, at your own pace.

pages.heading: Supplies with a place
pages.body: Kitchens and cellars may hold prepared food, farms may hold seeds, camps may hold camping supplies, and mining sites may hold rail supplies. Small additions accompany the normal chest loot. Opened chests are not restocked.

pages.heading: Enchanted travel wings
pages.body: More Enchantments flight effects recognize usable wings in Elytra Slot, including Iron and Leaden Wings. If usable wings also occupy your chest slot, those take priority. Each check uses one wing stack; durability stays on the selected wings.

pages.heading: Maintain your equipment
pages.body: Easy Anvils removes this pack's Too Expensive limit and softens repeated repair penalties. JRFTL supplies the existing rotten-flesh-to-leather route. Use these workshop options and JEI before discarding useful equipment; no extra salvage recipe is needed.
